messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testNestedWithCommentsJDOM` is failing because the JXPath library trims string values when retrieving text content from XML nodes, causing leading and trailing spaces in the original XML to be lost. This is evidenced by the current bug report describing how values with leading or trailing spaces, such as `<value> 12324 56</value>`, are returned without those spaces by JXPath.

The test calls `doTest("nested-with-comments", DocumentContainer.MODEL_JDOM, "foo;bar; baz ");` which internally creates a `JXPathContext` for the JDOM model and asserts that the value retrieved from the XPath expression matches the expected value with trailing spaces.

Inspecting the `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()` method reveals the root cause: for nodes such as `Element`, `Text`, `CDATA`, the method calls `getTextTrim()`, which explicitly trims whitespace from the text. For `Comment` and `ProcessingInstruction` nodes, it calls `getText()` or `getData()`, but then calls `trim()` on the resulting string.

Thus, no matter the node type, the value returned by `getValue()` in this class discards leading and trailing whitespace. This causes JXPath to "automatically trim string values," as described in the bug report, and leads to the failing test which expects whitespace to be preserved.

Since the test exercises the JDOM model, and the trimming is hardcoded in `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()`, this method is the likely source of the bug. It should not trim the text content if preserving whitespace is expected behavior.

No recent bug reports were found that contradict or supplement this conclusion.

Hence, the diagnosis is that `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()` trims text nodes erroneously, leading to loss of leading/trailing whitespace in JXPath string values, causing the test to fail and matching the described bug symptoms.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
